cases.purpose: Exercise target-path observations across same-directory replacement publication.
cases.distinct_invariant: A coordinated concurrent observer sees the complete original and then the complete validated replacement, never missing, partial, or unknown bytes.
cases.expected_result: The target remains continuously readable as one of the two complete validated states on the tested platform and filesystem.

cases.purpose: Exercise public fault injection at every publication stage with permission and cleanup checks.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every prepublication fault retains the permission-preserving original and no private file; the directory-sync fault reports the complete permission-preserving replacement as published.
cases.expected_result: Each structured stage result corresponds to exactly one complete file state and leaves no private-copy entry.

cases.purpose: Exercise an adversarial validator that replaces the already-validated private pathname before publication.
cases.distinct_invariant: Publication and cleanup both compare the pathname with the retained file identity, preserving the original and refusing to unlink the substituted unowned entry.
cases.expected_result: The operation fails at publication with cleanup refusal context, the target stays byte-identical, and the substituted bytes remain unpublished and undeleted.

cases.purpose: Verify deterministic machine-readable generic-signature and candidate-geometry output.
cases.distinct_invariant: A documented generic signature and aligned length yield only 2 KiB candidate arithmetic plus explicit non-claims.
cases.expected_result: JSON reports the signature kind, candidate geometry, no scan, and all required caveats.

cases.purpose: Verify unknown signature handling does not make format or compatibility claims.
cases.distinct_invariant: An aligned file without a documented generic Jet signature is rejected before geometry is reported.
cases.expected_result: The CLI emits deterministic error JSON and a failure status.

cases.purpose: Verify explicitly bounded raw page scanning, checksum stability, and complete algorithm-work accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: A scan within both supplied ceilings reads each candidate page exactly once and charges every hashed byte as explicit work in addition to page visits.
cases.expected_result: Repeated scans produce identical JSON and report exact page, byte, hash-work, and total-work counts.

cases.purpose: Verify independent raw-scan byte and page ceilings before page reads.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source exceeding either explicit ceiling is rejected by preflight.
cases.expected_result: Each insufficient ceiling produces its specific deterministic JSON error.

cases.purpose: Verify the CLI consumes the allocation-free raw page stream through the complete candidate geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: A three-page candidate is streamed exactly once from page zero through page two under exact explicit byte and page ceilings.
cases.expected_result: JSON reports three pages, 6,144 bytes, 6,144 hash-work units, and 6,147 total work units.

cases.purpose: Property-check every fixed-width writer primitive through the independently implemented binary cursor.
cases.distinct_invariant: All generated signed, unsigned, and floating bit patterns encode in explicit little-endian order and decode to the original bits under separate read accounting.
cases.expected_result: Every value, final position, remaining capacity, encoded-byte total, and aggregate-work total matches the generated reference stream.

cases.purpose: Property-check exact writes against an independent fixed-capacity and cumulative-budget model.
cases.distinct_invariant: For generated output sizes, positions, payloads, and limits, success occurs exactly when complete capacity and both budget dimensions allow it.
cases.expected_result: Successful writes change only the exact destination range and charge exact work; every rejected write preserves all bytes, position, and counters.

cases.purpose: Property-check typed byte offset and count arithmetic against Rust's checked u64 reference operations.
cases.distinct_invariant: For bounded deterministic edge and arbitrary u64 pairs, typed addition and subtraction succeed exactly when checked u64 arithmetic succeeds and return the same value.
cases.expected_result: No checked typed operation wraps, panics, or disagrees with the u64 reference result.

cases.purpose: Property-check format-neutral page partitioning across bounded aligned lengths and page sizes.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every generated aligned geometry partitions its complete source into contiguous non-overlapping ranges and rejects references at and above its page count.
cases.expected_result: All valid ranges exactly cover the source and every generated boundary reference is rejected structurally.

cases.purpose: Property-check malformed zero-size and partial-page geometry inputs.
cases.distinct_invariant: Zero page size is always invalid and every non-divisible source length reports its exact generated trailing byte count.
cases.expected_result: Malformed geometry is rejected without division by zero, truncation, wrapping, or panic.

cases.purpose: Property-check every fixed-width cursor primitive against standard little-endian encoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: All generated signed, unsigned, and floating primitive bit patterns round-trip through the bounded cursor in exact byte order.
cases.expected_result: Decoded values, floating bits, final position, remaining length, and charged work all match the generated reference stream.

cases.purpose: Property-check slice random access against an independent checked range and read-budget model.
cases.distinct_invariant: For every bounded generated source, range, and budget, success, failure class, output mutation, and charged bytes agree with the model, including u64 offset overflow.
cases.expected_result: Only valid budgeted ranges copy bytes and charge work; every rejected request preserves its destination and budget.

cases.purpose: Property-check raw fixed-size page mapping and operation-wide resource bounds over generated aligned byte sources.
cases.distinct_invariant: A generated page read succeeds exactly when read, page-reference, page-visit, and aggregate-work bounds all permit it, using one persistent operation budget.
cases.expected_result: Successful reads return the exact generated page and charge one read and visit; all preflight rejections preserve output and counters.

cases.purpose: Property-check candidate inspection composed with a commit-region snapshot over generated aligned sources.
cases.distinct_invariant: All generated commit-region bytes and two-byte slot order survive the candidate ownership boundary without normalization or semantic inference.
cases.expected_result: The generic signature kind, page geometry, complete raw region, pair classifications, and exact 527-byte read accounting agree with the generated model.

cases.purpose: Property-check candidate inspection, one raw page read, and a commit-region snapshot through one operation budget.
cases.distinct_invariant: The independently returned raw page and commit snapshot expose identical generated region bytes while every read, page visit, and work unit remains cumulative.
cases.expected_result: All returned bytes agree and the shared budget reports exactly 2,575 read bytes, one page visit, and one aggregate work unit.

cases.purpose: Property-check atomic commit snapshot publication after candidate inspection has consumed part of the cumulative read budget.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every generated remaining capacity below 512 bytes rejects the complete commit-region request without replacing the caller snapshot or erasing prior accounting.
cases.expected_result: The destination remains byte-for-byte unchanged and the shared operation retains exactly the successful 15-byte inspection charge with no page or aggregate work.

cases.purpose: Property-check allocation-free sequential page transfer against generated aligned candidate bytes.
cases.distinct_invariant: For every generated one-through-sixteen-page candidate, each yielded page number and complete byte array matches the corresponding physical source chunk in order.
cases.expected_result: The stream exhausts exactly at page count and cumulative signature, read, visit, and work accounting matches the generated model.

cases.purpose: Property-check cumulative read rejection at every generated complete-page boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A total-read budget allowing only a generated strict prefix yields exactly that prefix and rejects the next page without advancing the cursor.
cases.expected_result: Cursor position and all counters remain at the last successfully yielded page after the rejected request.

cases.purpose: Verify detached allocation-map record shape rejection without semantic traversal.
cases.distinct_invariant: Empty, short type-0, misaligned type-1, and unsupported records return their exact structured error after one bounded shape-inspection charge.
cases.expected_result: Every malformed or unsupported caller-delimited shape is rejected before iteration with exactly one work unit.

cases.purpose: Verify type-0 little-endian start-page and low-bit-first bitmap decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: Set bits one and seven yield start-page offsets one and seven while every inspected set or clear bit is charged.
cases.expected_result: The iterator yields pages 11 and 17 and consumes eight item units plus the one decoder work unit.

cases.purpose: Verify only emitted type-0 page references are geometry-validated.
cases.distinct_invariant: Clear bits extending beyond the supplied geometry are inspected and charged but never converted into rejected page references.
cases.expected_result: Only page zero is yielded and all sixteen bitmap bits are charged without an out-of-bounds error.

cases.purpose: Verify geometry validation of emitted type-0 page references.
cases.distinct_invariant: A set bit outside the supplied page count returns its exact structured boundary error after charging the inspected bits and then exhausts the cursor.
cases.expected_result: Page one is rejected against one-page geometry after two item charges and no later value is emitted.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic item-work rejection during type-0 bitmap inspection.
cases.distinct_invariant: A denied third bit remains pending and can be inspected with the same cursor under a replacement operation budget.
cases.expected_result: The constrained budget remains at two units and the resumed cursor yields the pending page with one new charge.

cases.purpose: Verify lossless type-1 raw little-endian reference decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: Zero, duplicate, and maximum u32 references are yielded unchanged without assigning null semantics or following them.
cases.expected_result: All four raw values round-trip in order with four item charges plus the one decoder work unit.

cases.purpose: Verify a caller-delimited type-1 record with no complete entries remains an empty detached shape.
cases.distinct_invariant: The type byte alone creates an exhausted raw-reference cursor without inferring a missing or null pointer.
cases.expected_result: The cursor returns no reference under a zero-item budget; only the decoder's one shape-inspection work unit is consumed.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic item-work rejection during type-1 raw-reference inspection.
cases.distinct_invariant: A denied raw reference remains pending and can be decoded under a replacement operation budget.
cases.expected_result: The zero-item budget stays unchanged and the resumed cursor yields raw reference 42.

cases.purpose: Verify bounded low-bit-first decoding of an already-classified complete Jet 3 type-05 page.
cases.distinct_invariant: Only byte zero classification gates decoding; bytes one through three remain uninterpreted and set bits are returned solely as relative indices across all 16,352 documented bitmap positions.
cases.expected_result: Relative indices zero and 16,351 are yielded with exact per-bit accounting and no absolute page-base claim.

cases.purpose: Verify detached extended-bitmap decoding requires the named byte-zero page classification.
cases.distinct_invariant: A complete data page is rejected before any bitmap bit is interpreted or charged.
cases.expected_result: The error retains the actual Data classification and only the prior classification work unit is present.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic item-work rejection during extended bitmap inspection.
cases.distinct_invariant: A denied second bit remains pending and can be inspected by the same cursor under a replacement operation budget.
cases.expected_result: The constrained budget stops at one unit and the resumed cursor yields relative bit one with one new charge.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic work-budget rejection before detached record inspection.
cases.distinct_invariant: A zero total-work limit rejects the decoder's one-unit shape inspection before reading or classifying the record.
cases.expected_result: The structured total-work error reports one requested unit while item and aggregate-work counters remain zero.

cases.purpose: Verify every format-specific traversal step stays blocked on evidence rather than guessed.
cases.distinct_invariant: Locating a map record and following raw references zero, one, and u32::MAX each return their structured unsupported step after exactly one explicit work unit.
cases.expected_result: No database page is read and no reference is interpreted.

cases.purpose: Verify bounded following of caller-supplied pages with exact accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: Two distinct extended bitmap pages are followed after a one-byte visited set was charged; each step charges one explicit unit, one page visit, and one classification, relative bits iterate, and absolute page derivation stays unsupported.
cases.expected_result: Depth equals two and every aggregate work unit is accounted for exactly.

cases.purpose: Verify repeat detection is structured, charged, and non-destructive.
cases.distinct_invariant: Following an already followed page charges one page visit, returns RepeatedPage, and leaves depth and the visited set unchanged so a later distinct page still follows.
cases.expected_result: Depth advances only on the distinct page.

cases.purpose: Verify out-of-range pages are rejected before any read.
cases.distinct_invariant: A page at the captured page count returns InvalidReference carrying the page and PageOutOfBounds source.
cases.expected_result: Page visits and depth are unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify a followed page must carry the required classification.
cases.distinct_invariant: A documented data page and an unknown-tag page each return UnexpectedPageKind with their lossless PageKind and are not marked as followed; the data page then follows when data is required.
cases.expected_result: Unknown tag 0x7f is retained without interpretation.

cases.purpose: Verify the chain-depth ceiling is exact and precedes reads.
cases.distinct_invariant: With a maximum chain depth of one, the first page follows and the second is rejected with a ChainDepth resource error.
cases.expected_result: Page visits and depth do not change on the rejected step.

cases.purpose: Verify visited-set storage is charged through the budget before allocation.
cases.distinct_invariant: A ten-page geometry needs two visited bytes; a one-byte allocation ceiling rejects construction with AllocationBytes and leaves zero bytes charged, while a two-byte ceiling succeeds and charges exactly two.
cases.expected_result: No visited set is allocated when the charge is rejected.

cases.purpose: Verify a resource rejection leaves the walker exactly as it was.
cases.distinct_invariant: With page visits exhausted, following a page returns a PageVisits read resource error without marking the page or advancing depth, and the same page follows under a fresh budget.
cases.expected_result: Depth is zero after rejection and one after the retry.

cases.purpose: Verify the visited set never grows past its reserved geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: Marking reports first and repeat insertions exactly, and a page at the page count is rejected with PageOutOfBounds.
cases.expected_result: Membership queries outside the range are false and allocation is fixed.

cases.purpose: Verify copy work limits immediately around the configured boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: Atomic copy work accepts one below and exact capacity and rejects one above.
cases.expected_result: Boundary outcomes are structured and the original remains safe.

cases.purpose: Verify the post-publication directory-sync failure classification.
cases.distinct_invariant: A directory-sync fault after rename reports that a validated replacement was published.
cases.expected_result: The published state is reported without claiming the original remains active.

cases.purpose: Verify every injected failure before publication.
cases.distinct_invariant: Each prepublication fault preserves original bytes and removes the private copy.
cases.expected_result: No partial replacement is exposed at any injected stage.

cases.purpose: Verify mutation and validation callback failures.
cases.distinct_invariant: Mutation and replacement-validation errors leave the original unchanged.
cases.expected_result: The callback error is structured and original bytes are preserved.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic update target preconditions.
cases.distinct_invariant: Missing and non-regular targets are rejected before private-copy mutation.
cases.expected_result: A structured target error is returned without publication.

cases.purpose: Verify the successful atomic publication path.
cases.distinct_invariant: A validated replacement is published with the original permissions preserved.
cases.expected_result: The replacement is visible only after successful validation and publication.

cases.purpose: Verify cleanup-error reporting when a primary publication error already exists.
cases.distinct_invariant: A cleanup failure is retained as secondary context without replacing the primary atomic-update error.
cases.expected_result: The primary error remains authoritative while cleanup failure details stay observable.

cases.purpose: Fault-inject the first fallible operation after exclusive private-file creation.
cases.distinct_invariant: Private-path ownership is guarded before identity capture, so capture failure removes the newly created entry without touching the target.
cases.expected_result: The injected identity error is returned, the target remains unchanged, and no private entry leaks.

cases.purpose: Verify binary cursor input-size construction boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Binary cursor construction accepts exact input capacity and rejects one byte above.
cases.expected_result: Exact capacity succeeds and excess input returns a structured limit error.

cases.purpose: Verify cumulative accounting across repeated reads.
cases.distinct_invariant: Rereads consume cumulative budget and rejection does not advance cursor state.
cases.expected_result: The exhausted read fails with position and budget preserved.

cases.purpose: Verify zero-length reading at the input end.
cases.distinct_invariant: An empty read at end-of-input succeeds without charging work.
cases.expected_result: The cursor remains at the end with zero additional work.

cases.purpose: Verify successful exact-read accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: An exact read advances position and cumulative work by precisely its byte count.
cases.expected_result: Returned bytes, cursor position, and work total match the request.

cases.purpose: Verify oversized range rejection before allocation.
cases.distinct_invariant: A huge truncated range returns a structured error without allocating its claimed size.
cases.expected_result: The range fails safely with bounded work and no panic.

cases.purpose: Verify little-endian floating-point primitive decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: 32-bit and 64-bit floating reads preserve their exact IEEE bit patterns.
cases.expected_result: Decoded floating values reproduce the source bit representations.

cases.purpose: Verify signed and unsigned little-endian integer decoding.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every supported integer width decodes exactly in little-endian order.
cases.expected_result: Decoded integer values and cursor advancement match the input bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify the single-read boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A read one byte above the per-read limit fails without advancing position.
cases.expected_result: A structured single-read limit error preserves cursor state.

cases.purpose: Verify primitive truncation behavior.
cases.distinct_invariant: A truncated fixed-width primitive read propagates error without partial advancement.
cases.expected_result: The cursor position remains unchanged after structured truncation.

cases.purpose: Verify absolute seek boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Seeking to start or exact end succeeds while seeking past end is rejected.
cases.expected_result: Valid positions are retained and the invalid seek preserves prior state.

cases.purpose: Verify structured exact-read truncation details.
cases.distinct_invariant: Truncation reports the request offset, needed bytes, and available bytes exactly.
cases.expected_result: The returned error contains complete checked boundary context.

cases.purpose: Verify complete output-capacity preflight before mutation.
cases.distinct_invariant: A write one byte beyond remaining fixed capacity fails without changing output, position, or either budget counter.
cases.expected_result: The structured capacity error reports exact offset, need, and availability while every observable state remains unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify writer resource-policy rejection atomicity.
cases.distinct_invariant: Encoded-byte and aggregate-work ceilings are checked independently before any output or accounting mutation.
cases.expected_result: Each structured limit error identifies its rejected dimension and preserves bytes, position, encoded bytes, and total work.

cases.purpose: Verify exact output mutation and rewrite accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: Seeking backward and overwriting two bytes consumes two new encoded bytes and work units without discarding the original four-byte charge.
cases.expected_result: The output contains the exact rewrite and cumulative counters report six bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify writer construction, seek, remaining, and empty-write boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: The exact fixed-capacity end accepts seek and empty write while one byte past end is rejected without work.
cases.expected_result: Capacity and remaining are exact, bytes remain untouched, and the structured position error preserves state.

cases.purpose: Verify every writer primitive's exact byte representation.
cases.distinct_invariant: Signed and unsigned 8/16/32/64-bit values and selected floating NaN payloads encode in little-endian order without bit normalization.
cases.expected_result: The complete 42-byte output matches an independent literal and exact accounting.

cases.purpose: Verify bounded composition of generic signature and exact candidate geometry.
cases.distinct_invariant: Successful inspection reads exactly the fifteen-byte signature window, derives aligned 2 KiB geometry, and visits no pages.
cases.expected_result: The candidate reports its generic kind and geometry with fifteen read bytes and zero page or aggregate work.

cases.purpose: Verify deterministic candidate inspection error ordering.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source with both an unknown signature and partial geometry fails at signature recognition first.
cases.expected_result: The structured error identifies the signature stage after exactly one bounded signature read.

cases.purpose: Verify the second candidate inspection stage and its accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: A recognized generic signature with a one-byte partial page reports geometry only after the signature read succeeds.
cases.expected_result: The structured geometry error reports one trailing byte, fifteen read bytes, and zero page visits.

cases.purpose: Verify candidate inspection at one below its exact read boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A fourteen-byte single-read ceiling rejects the fifteen-byte signature request without charging any work.
cases.expected_result: The candidate returns the nested structured limit error with every counter unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify successful raw candidate page delegation.
cases.distinct_invariant: Reading the second raw page returns its exact bytes while sharing the persistent signature, read, page, and aggregate accounting.
cases.expected_result: The destination matches the source page and accounting records 15 plus 2,048 read bytes and one page visit.

cases.purpose: Verify out-of-range raw candidate reads are atomic.
cases.distinct_invariant: A page reference equal to page count fails before source access, destination mutation, or page-work charging.
cases.expected_result: The structured page-boundary error preserves the sentinel destination and all post-inspection counters.

cases.purpose: Verify raw candidate destination atomicity after an underlying I/O attempt.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source failure after read and page preflight retains the attempted accounting but never exposes a partial destination.
cases.expected_result: The nested I/O error preserves the sentinel destination while charging exactly one page attempt and its read bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify ownership access for inspected candidate sources.
cases.distinct_invariant: Borrowing and consuming a candidate both expose the original source with its captured length.
cases.expected_result: Both access paths report the exact single-page source length.

cases.purpose: Verify candidate diagnostics distinguish input-policy, signature, and geometry stages.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every public candidate inspection error variant has stage-specific display context and preserves its structured source.
cases.expected_result: Formatting identifies the failed stage and standard error chaining exposes the nested error.

cases.purpose: Verify candidate inspection preserves each generic signature classification from SRC-0004.
cases.distinct_invariant: Standard, system, and temporary signature windows all compose with the same exact 2 KiB candidate geometry without narrowing the claimed generation.
cases.expected_result: Every inspected candidate returns the corresponding generic Jet file kind after exactly fifteen read bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify candidate inspection does not interpret bytes outside its documented signature window.
cases.distinct_invariant: Mutating leading, immediately following, and final page bytes leaves generic classification and arithmetic geometry unchanged.
cases.expected_result: Inspection still reports the standard generic kind, one page, and exactly fifteen read bytes.

cases.purpose: Verify every candidate truncation before the complete signature window.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every source length from zero through eighteen fails structurally during signature access before geometry or page visitation.
cases.expected_result: Each truncation returns a nested bounded-read error with no read charge or page work.

cases.purpose: Verify the candidate's cumulative read boundary independently of its single-read boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A cumulative ceiling of fourteen rejects the fifteen-byte signature while the per-read ceiling permits it.
cases.expected_result: The nested total-read limit error leaves read and page counters unchanged.

cases.purpose: Verify arbitrary ReadAt implementations cannot bypass the operation input ceiling.
cases.distinct_invariant: Candidate inspection independently rejects a generic source one byte above its input policy before signature I/O or geometry.
cases.expected_result: The input-stage structured error is first and all work counters remain zero.

cases.purpose: Verify candidate geometry and raw page bounds remain tied to captured source length.
cases.distinct_invariant: Growth of underlying storage after source construction does not expose an added page through inspection or raw reads.
cases.expected_result: Geometry remains one page, the first page is readable, and the newly appended second page is out of bounds.

cases.purpose: Verify strict canonical snapshot ordering checks for all protocol-declared sequences.
cases.distinct_invariant: Tables, columns, indexes, rows, and relationships are each rejected when their declared canonical ordering is violated.
cases.expected_result: Every unordered sequence returns a structured error identifying its semantic path.

cases.purpose: Verify explicit canonicalization of every protocol-declared sequence.
cases.distinct_invariant: One explicit operation sorts tables, columns, indexes, rows, and relationships without changing undeclared sequence semantics.
cases.expected_result: Canonicalized state and canonicalized output have the exact declared ascending orders.

cases.purpose: Verify unique identity requirements enforced by the executable protocol validator.
cases.distinct_invariant: Duplicate table names, column ordinals or names, index names, and relationship names fail closed after sorting.
cases.expected_result: Every duplicate identity returns a structured error containing its semantic path and duplicated value.

cases.purpose: Verify Unicode code-point ordering of dynamic JSON object keys.
cases.distinct_invariant: ASCII, accented BMP, and supplementary-plane keys are emitted in Unicode code-point ascending order.
cases.expected_result: Canonical JSON places the representative keys in exact protocol order without ASCII escaping.

cases.purpose: Verify retention of protocol sequences that have no sorting declaration.
cases.distinct_invariant: Index fields, relationship field pairs, and raw-preservation records retain producer-declared order.
cases.expected_result: Canonical output preserves the exact supplied order of all three sequence kinds.

cases.purpose: Verify required nested string and collection constraints.
cases.distinct_invariant: Empty DAO types, index fields, relationship fields, raw semantic paths, and raw purposes are rejected at their precise locations.
cases.expected_result: Each malformed nested shape returns a structured empty-string or empty-collection error.

cases.purpose: Verify exact protocol constants, object-key order, compactness, and line termination for an empty snapshot.
cases.distinct_invariant: The minimal typed model emits the complete protocol 1.0.0 canonical snapshot byte sequence with one trailing LF.
cases.expected_result: Emitted bytes exactly equal the checked compact UTF-8 JSON document.

cases.purpose: Verify all fifteen canonical typed-value discriminants and representations.
cases.distinct_invariant: Every protocol value kind has a distinct kind tag and correctly typed semantic value, with optional fields in canonical key order.
cases.expected_result: Canonical output contains the exact representation for each typed value kind.

cases.purpose: Verify the required distinction among SQL null, empty text, and empty binary.
cases.distinct_invariant: The three semantically distinct values retain different typed canonical JSON despite having no content.
cases.expected_result: Null emits JSON null while text and binary emit empty strings under distinct kind tags.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical UTF-8 string escaping across controls, syntax characters, and non-ASCII scalars.
cases.distinct_invariant: Required controls are minimally escaped while accented and supplementary Unicode remain direct UTF-8.
cases.expected_result: The exact compact escape sequences are present without ASCII-only or surrogate escaping.

cases.purpose: Verify finite numeric normalization and non-finite rejection.
cases.distinct_invariant: Negative zero, fixed, scientific, and large integral finite values emit normalized JSON while NaN and infinities cannot enter the model.
cases.expected_result: Finite values have exact deterministic number text and all non-finite constructors return structured errors.

cases.purpose: Verify lowercase hexadecimal and hyphenated GUID grammar.
cases.distinct_invariant: Only even-length lowercase hexadecimal text and exact lowercase GUID shapes are constructible.
cases.expected_result: Valid boundary representations succeed and uppercase, odd, malformed, or non-hex inputs fail structurally.

cases.purpose: Verify invariant decimal, currency, and timezone-free date/time grammar.
cases.distinct_invariant: Accepted and rejected boundary strings match the executable protocol validator's representation rules.
cases.expected_result: Only invariant decimal and timezone-free ISO-shaped date/time strings are constructible.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot scenario, database hash, and producer revision boundaries.
cases.distinct_invariant: Scenario family grammar, lowercase SHA-256 length, and Unicode producer revision length are enforced before emission.
cases.expected_result: Accepted protocol boundaries construct exactly and every malformed identity returns its specific structured error.

cases.purpose: Verify deterministic canonical snapshot byte equality.
cases.distinct_invariant: Repeated strict serialization, clone serialization, and explicit canonicalized serialization produce identical retained bytes.
cases.expected_result: All three independently requested byte vectors are exactly equal.

cases.purpose: Verify canonical row ordering when producer-declared keys are not unique.
cases.distinct_invariant: Rows sharing one key sort by canonical values while semantically identical duplicate rows remain retained.
cases.expected_result: Strict emission rejects reversed values, explicit canonicalization orders them, and identical duplicates survive.

cases.purpose: Verify parsing of an explicitly byte- and page-bounded raw scan request.
cases.distinct_invariant: A scan request carrying both resource ceilings and an input ceiling is accepted by the command parser.
cases.expected_result: The bounded arguments produce a probe command without performing I/O.

cases.purpose: Verify scan-only resource options cannot silently alter a signature-only probe.
cases.distinct_invariant: A scan resource ceiling without the explicit scan flag is rejected.
cases.expected_result: Argument parsing returns the scan-not-requested error.

cases.purpose: Verify raw scans require independent byte and page ceilings.
cases.distinct_invariant: Omitting either explicit scan ceiling prevents all-page reading.
cases.expected_result: Argument parsing rejects each incomplete scan request before file access.

cases.purpose: Verify command output failures remain observable to the exit-status boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A writer that rejects output returns an I/O error instead of silently discarding the JSON contract.
cases.expected_result: The shared output helper propagates the injected write failure for conversion to a nonzero process exit.

cases.purpose: Verify exact bounded access to the Microsoft-documented Jet 3 commit region.
cases.distinct_invariant: The reader issues one 512-byte request at absolute offset 0x600 and exposes no bytes outside that interval.
cases.expected_result: The returned snapshot exactly matches bytes 0x600 through 0x7ff and the read budget is charged once.

cases.purpose: Verify the physical commit-region end boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source ending exactly at 0x800 is sufficient, and arbitrary bytes after 0x800 never affect the snapshot.
cases.expected_result: Every source returns the same complete 512-byte region regardless of trailing content.

cases.purpose: Verify every truncation before the documented commit-region boundary.
cases.distinct_invariant: All source lengths below 0x800 fail with exact offset or remaining-byte context before any read charge.
cases.expected_result: Each truncation returns the corresponding structured boundary error with zero consumed read work.

cases.purpose: Verify commit-region access at exact input and read ceilings.
cases.distinct_invariant: A single-read and cumulative-read ceiling of exactly 512 bytes admits one complete snapshot.
cases.expected_result: The reader succeeds and charges exactly the complete region length.

cases.purpose: Verify independent one-below commit-region read limits.
cases.distinct_invariant: Single-read and total-read ceilings of 511 each reject the 512-byte request without touching the source.
cases.expected_result: Each policy dimension returns its own structured limit error with unchanged work.

cases.purpose: Verify commit-region access shares cumulative operation read accounting.
cases.distinct_invariant: Prior read work is included when accepting the exact remaining 512 bytes or rejecting one byte below.
cases.expected_result: Exact cumulative capacity succeeds while one-below rejects without source access or partial charge.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot publication after an underlying short read.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source that mutates a private buffer and reports 17 bytes cannot partially replace the caller's destination.
cases.expected_result: The structured short-read error retains the sentinel destination while charging the attempted request.

cases.purpose: Verify snapshot publication after an underlying I/O fault.
cases.distinct_invariant: A source fault after partially mutating its private buffer never exposes those bytes through the destination.
cases.expected_result: The structured I/O error retains the sentinel destination and exact attempted-read accounting.

cases.purpose: Verify atomic destination replacement on complete commit-region reads.
cases.distinct_invariant: The destination transitions from its sentinel only after all 512 source bytes are available.
cases.expected_result: A successful read publishes the exact complete region in one observable result.
